title: [PMON] | ERR pmon#xcvrd: Exception occured at SfpStateUpdateTask thread due to KeyError('status')
author: Junchao-Mellanox
body:

#### Description

The issue is probably introduced by commit: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-platform-daemons/commit/56046dc36907c7e873911ef60e9193fe8717b12c. In this commit, it added several new fieds to TRANSECIVER_STATUS table. It casues a potential race condition:

- DomInfoUpdateTask would update TRANSECIVER_STATUS table by calling function `update_port_transceiver_status_table_hw`
- SfpStateUpdateTask would update TRANSECIVER_STATUS table by calling function `update_port_transceiver_status_table_sw`. It also  reads TRANSECIVER_STATUS table by line https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-platform-daemons/blob/03374b24ac049f6476690208b482c72a35c974df/sonic-xcvrd/xcvrd/xcvrd.py#L2144 and access the table data by line https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-platform-daemons/blob/03374b24ac049f6476690208b482c72a35c974df/sonic-xcvrd/xcvrd/xcvrd.py#L2155

So, there could be chance that, DomInfoUpdateTask has called update_port_transceiver_status_table_hw, but SfpStateUpdateTask  has not called update_port_transceiver_status_table_sw. In that case, 'status' would not exist in TRANSECIVER_STATUS table which causes a crash.

Not sure that updating the same table from different threads is a good idea, but as the change in https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-platform-daemons/commit/56046dc36907c7e873911ef60e9193fe8717b12c is big, I would recommend to fix the issue in `SfpStateUpdateTask::on_add_logical_port` if we don't want to revert that change.

#### Steps to reproduce the issue:
Use dynamic port breakout CLI to split port, there is a **small chance** to hit this issue.

#### Describe the results you received:

xcvrd crashed:
```
Mar  9 01:26:48.894733 sonic ERR pmon#xcvrd: Exception occured at SfpStateUpdateTask thread due to KeyError('status')
Mar  9 01:26:48.896630 sonic ERR pmon#xcvrd: Traceback (most recent call last):
Mar  9 01:26:48.896630 sonic ERR pmon#xcvrd:   File "/usr/local/lib/python3.9/dist-packages/xcvrd/xcvrd.py", line 2049, in run
Mar  9 01:26:48.896720 sonic ERR pmon#xcvrd:     self.task_worker(self.task_stopping_event, self.sfp_error_event)
Mar  9 01:26:48.896732 sonic ERR pmon#xcvrd:   File "/usr/local/lib/python3.9/dist-packages/xcvrd/xcvrd.py", line 1862, in task_worker
Mar  9 01:26:48.896757 sonic ERR pmon#xcvrd:     port_mapping.handle_port_config_change(sel, asic_context, stopping_event, self.port_mapping, helper_logger, self.on_port_config_change)
Mar  9 01:26:48.896778 sonic ERR pmon#xcvrd:   File "/usr/local/lib/python3.9/dist-packages/xcvrd/xcvrd_utilities/port_mapping.py", line 225, in handle_port_config_change
Mar  9 01:26:48.896799 sonic ERR pmon#xcvrd:     read_port_config_change(asic_context, port_mapping, logger, port_change_event_handler)
Mar  9 01:26:48.896820 sonic ERR pmon#xcvrd:   File "/usr/local/lib/python3.9/dist-packages/xcvrd/xcvrd_utilities/port_mapping.py", line 244, in read_port_config_change
Mar  9 01:26:48.896837 sonic ERR pmon#xcvrd:     port_change_event_handler(port_change_event)
Mar  9 01:26:48.896869 sonic ERR pmon#xcvrd:   File "/usr/local/lib/python3.9/dist-packages/xcvrd/xcvrd.py", line 2082, in on_port_config_change
Mar  9 01:26:48.896869 sonic ERR pmon#xcvrd:     self.on_add_logical_port(port_change_event)
Mar  9 01:26:48.896869 sonic ERR pmon#xcvrd:   File "/usr/local/lib/python3.9/dist-packages/xcvrd/xcvrd.py", line 2155, in on_add_logical_port
Mar  9 01:26:48.896904 sonic ERR pmon#xcvrd:     logical_port_event_dict[port_change_event.port_name] = dict(sfp_status)['status']
Mar  9 01:26:48.896936 sonic ERR pmon#xcvrd: KeyError: 'status'
Mar  9 01:26:48.897069 sonic ERR pmon#xcvrd: Xcvrd: exception found at child thread SfpStateUpdateTask due to KeyError('status')
Mar  9 01:26:48.897069 sonic ERR pmon#xcvrd: Exiting main loop as child thread raised exception!
```


#### Describe the results you expected:

xcvrd should not crash

<!-- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

#### Description
Fix issue https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/14213.

https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-platform-daemons/commit/56046dc36907c7e873911ef60e9193fe8717b12c introduces a race condition between DomInfoUpdateTask and SfpStateUpdateTask. In this PR, `SfpStateUpdateTask::on_add_logical_port` is changed to no longer depending on TRANSECIVER_STATUS table and always get SFP data from platform API.

#### Motivation and Context
Fix https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/14213

> > If you are talking about CMIS manager, Nvidia platform does not use it. CMIS manager is disabled on Nvidia platform. Why do you think DPB and CMIS manager is related this PR? It is all about race condition while removing and adding logical port.
> 
> Thanks for the update. Reason I asked: In its git issue, you mentioned "steps to reproduce the issue" Use dynamic port breakout CLI to split port, there is a small chance to hit this issue.
> 
> So, looking for following UT test case (steps). could you attach the following data to this PR?
> 
> 1. snippet of platform.json and hwsku.json for the interface where DPB CLI was issued
> 2. config DB snippet for the interface (before issuing DPB CLI)
> 3. DPB CLI issued
> 4. config DB snippet for this interface (after issuing DPB CLI)
> 5. syslog etc. traces (esp. syncd) showing removal (of existing ports) and creation of new logical/sub-ports
> 6. syslog etc. traces for xcvrd flow for this scenario

Hi @shyam77git, 

1. The issue is not related to platform.json or hwsku.json. It is just related to adding/removing logical port. DPB CLI will remove the existing logic port and create new ones no matter what platform.json/hwsku.json is. You can use `config interface breakout <interface> <mode>` on ANY interface with ANY valid mode to reproduce the issue, but you may need to run it in a while loop for few hours to hit the race condition.
2. I found the root cause not by analyzing the syslog. Actually, there is no clue in the syslog. I found the issue by reading the code. So, I am not sure that providing the trace is helpful to understand the issue. 

Example, say we are going to break Ethernet0 to (Ethernet0 and Ethernet2)  :
1. It removes Ethernet0 first, `TRANSCEIVER_STATUS|Ethernet0` will be removed from TRANSCEIVER_STATUS table
2. It adds Ethernet0 back to CONFIG_DB, both SfpStateUpdateTask and DomInfoUpdateTask notice the new logic port.  SfpStateUpdateTask and DomInfoUpdateTask run in two different thread. So, there could be 2 possible cases:
  a. SfpStateUpdateTask get port add event first. No issue for this flow.
  b. DomInfoUpdateTask get port add event first. This flow causes issue. See below.

Let discuss case b:
1. DomInfoUpdateTask get port add event first. It calls update_port_transceiver_status_table_hw which will populate a few data to `TRANSCEIVER_STATUS|Ethernet0`, but it does not populate "status" field.
2. Then, SfpStateUpdateTask gets new port add event. It calls on_port_config_change -> on_add_logical_port and hit the line:
```
        logical_port_event_dict[port_change_event.port_name] = dict(sfp_status)['status']   <===== crash because 'status' is not a valid key in dict(sfp_status)
```

`TRANSCEIVER_STATUS|Ethernet0` has no 'status' field yet, so the above line get an KeyError and crashes. 

I hope this is clear now.
